The scene changes every 6 to 8 seconds across 6 setups, and the last line returns to the hook phrase, so there is a reason to stay to the end (inferred; no retention data is in meta.json).
paid_signal: no: like_rate 5.14% is high and the account median is only 2,242 views, which looks like organic viral spread, not bought reach (inference).

solo_route.how: 1) Write a 40 to 45 second Hebrew script of 8 to 10 short Q-and-A jokes about a baby's first day, kid-safe, with the last line pointing to the baby's own book. 2) Generate 5 or 6 clips of about 6 to 8 seconds each with a text-to-video or image-to-video tool: baby in hallway, in a crib, in a basket outdoors, on a street, and a final clip of a baby with a LumeBook book. Use a fictional mic with LumeBook branding, not a TV channel name. 3) Add an AI or your own pitched-up voice for the baby and a second voice for the reporter, and line up the audio over the clips in CapCut. 4) Add Hebrew burned-in captions and one emoji row. About 2 to 4 hours of generation and retries.
solo_route.needs: A clean script and a decision on voices (no cloned real-person or celebrity voices). Do not copy the swearing, the paternity or skin-colour punchline, or the fake 'Channel 8' mic.

evidence_notes: SPOKEN: Whisper transcript is full English and matches the caption quote ('i need to go back in, my parents are broke as 💩'), so medium to high reliability for content, but its segment timings are coarse (it ends at 47.2s on a 46.05s video) and I placed lines against scenes approximately. I cannot tell whether the voice is synthetic or human. OBSERVED: the 16:9 clip sits letterboxed in a 9:16 black canvas with a row of seven 😂 emojis above; 'Channel 8' reads on the mic flag at 6.0 to 12.0s. AI-LOOKS (my read, not certain): a different baby in every scene (6 scenes, no character continuity); babies sit upright and hold their necks steady (a newborn cannot at this age); a newborn at 24.0s and a beanie baby at 30.0s have defined abdominal and arm muscle ridges; the beanie baby stands unsupported on a busy street. Frame sampling is 2s, so I cannot check lip-sync or morphing between frames. No tool is named in the caption or text (#ai only). LIKENESS/CONSENT: the babies look synthetic and I see no real identifiable person; I cannot rule out that any was built from a real child's photo. 'Channel 8' mimics a TV news brand, and the final shot (spoken line about being 'supposed to come out white' over a darker-skinned baby) relies on a skin-colour or paternity joke, which is a brand-safety problem for LumeBook. made_by is 'unclear': a personal account with no credit or watermark, so I cannot say whether the owner generated it or reposted it.
